title: void.json
description: The manifest every Void project carries at its root. The build-time twin of --describe: --describe answers 'what can I do?' at runtime, this answers 'what am I, and what do I need?' before anything is built.

manifest.description: Format version, so this file can change later without breaking readers.

name.description: Machine name, lowercase, no spaces. The identity Mago resolves against.

kind.description: Sorted by what a user experiences, not by how the code is shaped. A runtime is never a row in anybody's list of installed software; an application always is.

version.description: Three parts. Below 1.0 the minor position is the break: 0.2.7 and 0.2.12 promise compatibility, 0.2.x and 0.3.0 do not.

requires.description: Real dependency edges. Mago resolves these, and `link` is the field that decides whether an upstream change costs a rebuild or only a re-ship.

version.description: A floor or `*`. Mago intersects every constraint on a project and reports which one actually binds.

sibling.description: Relative path to the checkout during development, e.g. ../VoidCore.

cmake_var.description: The variable a resolver sets to point a build at a specific checkout, without editing anybody's CMakeLists.txt.

link.description: How the dependency is bound in, which is the field that decides what an upstream change costs. shared: a file ships beside the binary, and an additive change costs only a re-ship. static/source/vendored: the code is inside the consumer's build output, so any upstream change costs a rebuild, transitively. import: the consumer imports the dependency's source at runtime, the way a Python package imports another -- nothing is compiled and nothing of the dependency's ships, so an additive change is a retest and a breaking one is a port. Use `import` and not `source` for an interpreted consumer: `source` claims a binary that does not exist.

via.description: Reached through another project's headers rather than directly.

interacts_with.description: NOT dependencies. Data crosses, nothing links: a transcript one project emits and another replays, a conformance case format, a bundle. Recorded separately so the compatibility matrix does not invent edges that do not exist. A seam costs a retest, never a rebuild.

seam.description: What the two ends actually exchange. Both ends should call it the same thing; `mago doctor` reports it when they disagree.

documents.description: Document formats this project DEFINES, as label -> filename or glob. Ownership, not merely use: a seam named after one of these is a contract that can break when THIS project changes, and nothing at all when its readers do. That is what keeps `mago blast voidcore` from reporting a retest for every project that reads a void.json.

artifacts.description: Prebuilt files a shared-link consumer ships. Name the platform in the filename; Mago matches on it.

ships_beside_binary.description: Folders and files that must land next to the executable. A trailing / means a folder, copied recursively.

vendors.description: Third-party code this project uses and does not own. `requires` is a Void project; this is everything else -- cJSON, SQLite, GLFW, Dear ImGui, libsodium, and the toolchain runtime that arrives whether anybody asked for it or not. The family vendors rather than resolves, and that rule was doing two jobs: deciding how third-party code is ACQUIRED (copied in, pinned, reviewed) and quietly deciding it need not be WRITTEN DOWN. Only the first was a good idea. Not called a `holiday`: Void Core's holiday is a runtime interface to an external SYSTEM, where all real I/O lives, and vendored source has no interface and no I/O.

name.description: As its authors spell it: `cJSON`, `Dear ImGui`. Grouped case- and punctuation-insensitively across the family, so drift cannot hide behind a spelling.

version.description: Free text: third-party versions are not all semver. Its value is comparison against the other copies in the family, so any stable spelling works as long as everybody uses the same one.

license.description: SPDX where there is one. Without it the library cannot appear in a notices file, and a notices file is a legal obligation rather than a nicety.

path.description: Where the vendored copy lives, relative to this repository. One entry covers a library's several files: `vendor/cJSON.c` accounts for `vendor/cJSON.h` beside it.

version_source.description: A file in this repository carrying the upstream's own version literal, for `mago doctor` to check the declared version against. Matched either literally (`"3.45.1"`) or split across macros the way cJSON writes it (MAJOR 1 / MINOR 7 / PATCH 18).

link.description: How it reaches the consumer's binary. source/static/vendored/header-only are compiled in and ship no file of their own. shared ships a file. system is provided by the operating system and must NOT ship. toolchain comes from the compiler and is the dangerous one: it exists on the build machine and on no other, so it must be linked statically or shipped deliberately -- Void Hormiga's first package would have gone out without `libwinpthread-1.dll` for exactly this reason.

release.description: What THIS version did, declared by the person who did it. Everything else in a manifest is a standing fact; this block is the only part that describes an event. It exists because every verdict in a release broadcast is derivable from the manifests plus ONE fact a human supplies -- whether the change was additive or breaking -- and that one bit is a field a release can declare. With it, `mago blast <project>` needs no flags and `mago notify <project>` can write the whole broadcast.

version.description: The version this release produced. Defaults to, and must equal, the manifest's own `version`.

previous.description: What consumers are moving FROM. Without it, blast and notify still need --to.

change.description: The one bit of judgement no manifest can derive. Omitted, it is inferred from the version numbers under the family's below-1.0 rule -- and an inference about a promise is a guess.

summary.description: One line. It becomes the headline of every message this release sends.

adds.description: New OPTIONAL surface: verbs, fields, files. Nobody must adopt any of it and no verdict changes if they do not -- but a resolver has nothing to say here and a notifier does.

behavior_changes.description: Things that moved WITHOUT a signature moving. The category a dependency resolver structurally cannot see, and the one that bites: no version constraint is violated, every verdict stays correct, and a consumer breaks anyway. Each entry is an OBJECT; Mago refuses a bare string by name rather than skipping it, because a behavior change that is quietly absent is the warning that never arrived.

read_more.description: Where the argument is written down. Paths relative to this repository; a message rewrites them relative to whoever receives it.

version_sources.description: Which files in this repository state the same version, for `mago doctor` to check the manifest against. Absent means the well-known ones (CMakeLists.txt, pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml). Present -- including present and empty -- is the project's own answer, for a repository that versions a subcomponent separately. Worth checking: Void Core shipped 0.2.14 with a void.json reading 0.2.12, and every verdict about a project is arithmetic over that number.

side_by_side.description: A new version never destroys a working one. True everywhere in this family.
